mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy that typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs reduce corporate investments and consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when RSAFS increases by >2% YoY, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases > 1% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When Housing Starts (HOUST) and Real Final Sales (RSAFS) both increase by more than 2% month-over-month, it signals a broad-based demand surge, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy is seen as robust.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 2% MoM
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when both HOUST and RSAFS increase > 2% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% month-over-month, it signals a tightening labor market, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates strong economic growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% MoM
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When Industrial Production (INDPRO) and Capacity Utilization (not available in catalog) both show a month-over-month increase, it signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases > 1% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.
